code_style: AI-code. AI-generated attributed scalar/chiral meson benchmark inputs.

publication.title: Theoretical analysis of the doubly radiative decays eta(') -> pi0 gamma gamma and eta' -> eta gamma gamma
publication.citation: Escribano et al., Phys. Rev. D 102, 034026 (2020)
publication.equations: Leading ChPT4-7; replacement linear-sigma amplitudes16-21; complete one-loop propagatorsA1-A7; component widthsTableII.

conventions.loop_isospin_masses: Charged pion and charged kaon masses are used throughout the charged loops and the isospin-symmetric scalar self energies. The observed neutral recoil mass is used in phase space. The primary does not print its complete numerical pseudoscalar input card; rounded TableII agreement is a control, not a precision fit.
conventions.scalar_width: First-sheet threshold-dependent one-loop self energies with on-shell real subtraction; no constant scalar Breit-Wigner widths.
conventions.matching: The linear-sigma amplitude replaces the ChPT strong amplitude. They must never be added as independent contributions.
conventions.photon_symmetry: The real-photon control includes the identical-photon factor1/2. A photon plus massive A-prime is distinguishable.

model_scope: Isospin-limit phenomenological linear-sigma plus separately supplied VMD model; not a complete all-orders QCD or effective-field-theory prediction.
Nonresonant crossed scalar exchange uses the primary's chiral-matched infinite-mass approximation, not explicit scalar exchange in t and u.
The helper supplies only strong four-pseudoscalar amplitudes; the calling electromagnetic-current model declares its own timelike continuation and retained operators.
Measured radiative branching ratios are not used as multiplicative corrections. The primary cannot reproduce all three measured widths simultaneously and reports that limitation.
Material transport, native recoil decay, weighted source normalization and the full detector/publication chain require independent qualification.
